title: How Guide Dogs Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how guide dogs work, covering their history (German WWI-veteran training academy in Potsdam, Dorothy Harris Eustace, Morris Frank and The Seeing Eye in Tennessee), rules of etiquette for approaching working dogs, the intersection and curb-stopping training, selective disobedience, the puppy raising program, intensive school training, graduation attrition, matching with handlers, and retirement. Also covers a brief dog-housebreaking tangent and listener mail asking the show to support Jane's knitting charity for Angels among Us Pet Rescue.

segments.title: Opening banter and guide dog origins
segments.summary: The hosts open with banter, then discuss the history of guide dogs: the German guide dog academy in Potsdam for WWI-blinded veterans, Dorothy Harris Eustace's article in the Saturday Evening Post, and Morris Frank founding The Seeing Eye school in Tennessee with her funding.

segments.title: Etiquette around guide dogs
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why people should not distract working guide dogs, the fact that a handler can say whether it is okay to pet the dog, and that guide dogs are generally allowed anywhere the public is allowed.

segments.title: Guide dog skills: crosswalks, curbs and selective disobedience
segments.summary: The dog must hold a direct route, stay just ahead and to the left of the handler, and master intersections and curbs. Dogs stop at every curb and will refuse a forward command when a hazard is present, a behavior called selective disobedience. The hosts also mention city crosswalk signals.

segments.title: Dog behavior, elevators, stairs and working versus pet life
segments.summary: The hosts discuss other required behaviors such as stopping at stairs, lying quietly, and not acting like a regular dog in public. They talk about whether guide dogs are sad, and how working dogs are happier and then playful as family pets once the harness comes off. They also digress on a pet dog named Lucy.

segments.title: Cost and structure of guide dog schools
segments.summary: Guide dog schools are nonprofits that provide dogs free of charge, handling breeding, puppy raising, training, instructor training, handler matching and retirement. Labs, Golden Retrievers and German Shepherds are common breeds, and self-confidence is a key trait.

segments.title: Housebreaking tangent
segments.summary: The hosts joke about a housebreaking method for puppies, saying to take the puppy to the same outdoor spot hourly, praise it when it goes, and add a verbal cue such as go potty, so it can go on command in public.

segments.title: Puppy raising program
segments.summary: Puppies are evaluated from around six weeks old, and many are weeded out. Volunteer puppy raisers raise dogs for about a year to a year and a half, teaching basic obedience and socialization through five new experiences a week, using praise and corrections rather than treats. Raisers return the dog to a school when it is time, and some get the dog back at retirement.
topics: returning puppy to guide dog school

segments.title: Intensive school training, graduation and handler matching
segments.summary: After puppy raising, dogs enter about six months of intensive school training on fake intersections, stairs and cliffs, learning to think at human height such as avoiding low beams. Only around a third of dogs graduate, and then handlers train for about a month to match with a dog. Instructors need supervised apprentice experience and the work is demanding but rewarding.

segments.title: Retirement of guide dogs
segments.summary: Guide dogs typically retire at about eight to ten years old. Handlers may keep them, or they may go back to the puppy raiser or to an adopter.

segments.title: Listener mail: Jane's knitting charity for Angels among Us
segments.summary: A listener, an ER doctor who runs a charity knitting site, says proceeds fund Angels among Us Pet Rescue in Alpharetta, Georgia, and asks listeners to support her goal of six thousand dollars. The hosts endorse the cause and promote the show's social channels and outro.
